label: canon-c19-in12-eager-q10-n2
_why: THE SPLIT TEST, RE-AIMED AT THE SPREAD (rewritten 2026-09-16 after config 1 read at n=2). canon-c19-in12-eager (session 20260915_232710) did BOTH halves of its job and they point opposite ways. It fixed the hoard in BOTH seeds - world pool 0.27 / 0.34 of GDP against the C 1.9 family's 0.42-0.70 and vanilla's 0.29, shortlist 0.14 / 0.40 against 0.61-1.50, Britain 0.15 / 0.22 against 0.87-2.40, the private backlog 0.8 y in both against 2.0-2.4 and the government's 0.8 / 1.3 against 2.8-3.0, with the pool smaller in ABSOLUTE terms on a 33% larger economy in the booming seed (capital at work, not a starved pool). And it DESTABILISED the economy: GDP 0.738x and 1.446x vanilla, workers per capita 0.526x and 0.854x, where the same slope without the set spans 1.04-1.13x and 0.64-0.70x over four seeds. Run 2 tripped the run-level stop at 1.41x, so that configuration ended at n=2. With F121's three seeds of the same define set (0.37 / 0.56 / 1.32x), five eager seeds now span 0.37-1.45x. ⚠ A reading taken after config 1's run 1 alone - that the queue-cap define CONSTRUCTION_MAX_NUM_PRODUCTION_BUILDING_CONSTRUCTIONS_SCALED, reverted to vanilla's 0.05, throttled the economy - was RETRACTED by run 2 (same cap, a 5,511-level construction sector, 1.45x). The define IS a hard cap on concurrent production-building construction (the game's own comment) and the eager schedule's rationale for reverting it was wrong about what it does; but it did not cause run 1's level. SO THIS BOOK NOW ASKS A DIFFERENT QUESTION: does the instability come from the three SPENDING thresholds or from the queue cap? It keeps the thresholds (TOO_LARGE_INVESTMENT_POOL_FACTOR 0.99, CRITICAL 1.25, EXCESSIVE 3.0) and leaves the cap at the canon's 0.1 - one define from canon-c19-in12-eager, three from the found config canon-c19-in12, so one book isolates both halves. In scope: AI defines only (the user ruled the balance-side hoard levers out on 2026-09-15 - no construction-method changes, no law-side pool modifiers).

_delta: Against canon-c19-in12-eager (config 1): CONSTRUCTION_MAX_NUM_PRODUCTION_BUILDING_CONSTRUCTIONS_SCALED 0.05 -> 0.1, nothing else. Against canon-c19-in12 (the found config, F117/F120): the three spending thresholds 0.9 -> 0.99, 0.9 -> 1.25, 1.5 -> 3.0, nothing else.

_predictions._structure: READ FOR SPREAD, NOT LEVEL. Config 1's two seeds landed 0.71 of GDP ratio apart; the base family's four sit within 0.09. The question is which of those two pictures this book resembles. Three outcomes, pre-registered.
_predictions.A_the_thresholds_are_safe: The two runs land WITHIN ~0.15 of each other on GDP ratio and ~0.10 on workers (i.e. the base family's tightness), in or near the band (0.85-1.20x), AND the hoard stays low - world pool 0.25-0.45, shortlist under 0.6, Britain under 1.0. THEN the three spending thresholds are the hoard fix and the queue cap carried the instability; this book is the new candidate configuration and the first in the sweep with a pool at or below vanilla AND a readable spread.
_predictions.B_the_thresholds_destabilise: The two runs land far apart again (>= 0.3 of GDP ratio), or one trips the run-level stop. THEN the instability is the spending thresholds themselves - faster spending is a positive feedback the raised thresholds stop damping - and the whole eager family is closed. The hoard then has NO in-scope lever that leaves a readable configuration, and by the 2026-09-15 scope ruling it becomes an accepted documented residual: reported every batch, never tuned again, keeping only its role in the capital-abundance void criterion.
_predictions.C_stable_but_hoarding: The two runs land together in band AND the hoard returns to 0.40-0.70 world with Britain above 1.0. THEN the queue cap was doing the hoard work after all and costs stability to use - same conclusion as B for the hoard, but the thresholds are exonerated and could be kept for the shorter queues alone.
_predictions.queues: the diagnostic that separates A from C: under A the backlogs stay short (0.8-1.5 y private) because the thresholds keep the sector large relative to the economy; under C they lengthen back toward 2 y once the restored cap lets more be queued. Read queue_series.mjs at 1900/1920/1935 in BOTH runs, never only the medians.
_predictions.obsolescence: rung 0 unchanged by this lever - staffing tracks the economy's size (config 1: 53.0% in its stalled seed, 41.6% in its booming one, base 45-47%), its level count still rising. The sharp books are the lever aimed at that.
_predictions.perf: row P total within +10% of the vanilla median; no crash expected, the feeder handles a mid-autosave CTD (L32).

_alignment: THE 2+1 RULE (user-ruled 2026-09-14, F114): after run 2, `node tools/testbed/ledger/alignment_check.mjs --arm <session>:canon-c19-in12-eager-q10` - world GDP and productive workers per capita at 1935 against the vanilla per-run median, five bands each; a pair fails an axis only in different bands AND >= 0.15 (GDP) / >= 0.10 (workers) apart. DIVERGENT => the _tb.json as its own session, the reading the median of three. PLUS THE RUN-LEVEL STOP: any run above x1.3 of vanilla's 1936 GDP ends the config. PLUS THE CAPITAL-ABUNDANCE FLAG: `capital_flags.mjs`, a shortlist-wide trip is a VOID (exit 4).
_comparison: THREE references, and the design's point is that it sits between two of them: vanilla n=18 for every ratio; canon-c19-in12 (F117 + F120, four seeds: GDP 1.04-1.13x, workers 0.64-0.70x, hoard 0.42-0.70 world / 0.61-1.50 shortlist, backlogs 2.0-2.4 / 2.8-3.0 y) one lever group away on the thresholds; canon-c19-in12-eager (F124, two seeds: GDP 0.74 / 1.45x, hoard 0.27 / 0.34, backlogs 0.8 y) one define away on the queue cap.
